body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Sunday, August 16, 2026, and we’re waking up to a warm morning with a high expected near 98°. Overnight, Kern County saw a serious wrong-way crash on Highway 99 that claimed three lives, and firefighters battled a palm tree fire that spread to an apartment complex in southeast Bakersfield. Let’s take a look at what happened while you were sleeping.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious incident unfolded around 12:44 a.m. on southbound Highway 99 north of 7th Standard Road, where a wrong-way driver in a white Honda Accord collided head-on with a white BMW 530i and a white Chevrolet Colorado. The Honda caught fire, and all three occupants inside died from their injuries. The driver and another occupant of the BMW sustained major injuries, while the two occupants in the Chevrolet escaped with minor injuries. Crews worked to extricate two patients from the wreckage, both of whom were walking and green-tagged. Meanwhile, around 9:16 p.m., a palm tree fire near Villalobos Street spread to the roof of a two-story apartment complex on Spice Way. Engine 7 took incident command as additional units rolled in to battle the flames. Elsewhere, officers staged on a possible shooting on Price Street that never materialized on the air, chased a DUI driver in a white BMW 5 Series east from the 33rd Street area, and responded to a long string of domestics and disturbances—including one at a Camellia Village apartment where a hole was punched in the wall.

## Today's weather

Today’s forecast calls for a high near 98° and a low around 72° tonight. It’s currently 86° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and air quality is moderate at an AQI of 64. We’re not tracking any active fires in the region at this time.

## Top stories

**According to 23ABC, three people are dead after a wrong-way, three-vehicle crash on Highway 99 early this morning.** California Highway Patrol Bakersfield reports that a white Honda Accord was traveling northbound in the southbound lanes on Highway 99, north of 7th Standard Road, when it collided with a white BMW 530i and a white Chevrolet Colorado around 12:44 a.m. The crash caused the Honda to catch fire, and all three occupants inside the vehicle died from their injuries. The driver and one other occupant of the BMW sustained major injuries, while the two occupants in the Chevrolet sustained minor injuries. Authorities say it is unknown whether alcohol or drugs were a factor in the crash.

**KGET 17 reports that a Kern County homeless recovery leader recently helped shape a national addiction toolkit for addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community.** Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, was among roughly 22 professionals from across the country who gathered in Washington, D.C., in the spring to work with the Trump administration, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the Department of Health and Human Services, and the nation’s drug czar to develop the toolkit. The toolkit outlines best practices for working with individuals dealing with addiction within the homeless population, covering topics including program length, transitional housing, long-term mentorship, and workforce development.

**23ABC tells us that Bakersfield’s police and fire chiefs presented their Fourth of July reports during a Friday meeting, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents in the city.** Bakersfield Fire Department Chief Kevin Albertson said the holiday brought serious consequences for people across the state, with some being significantly injured or killed by fireworks. A total of 106 citations were issued by the Bakersfield Police and Fire departments combined in relation to the holiday. Compared to 2025, fire-related responses to both departments dropped 6% in 2026. Despite the decrease, residents and officials say more work remains, and Bakersfield City Councilman Eric Arias said stronger policies are in the works to deter the use of illegal fireworks.

## Something good

Bakersfield and Tehachapi airports are set to receive a portion of $109 million in federal aviation funding. This financial support will help enhance local airport infrastructure and services, benefiting our community and supporting our local economy.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets on Tuesday, August 18, at 12:00 p.m. The Historic Preservation Commission convenes on Tuesday, August 18, at 4:00 p.m., while the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission meets on Tuesday, August 18, at 2:00 p.m. The Water Board meets on Wednesday, August 19, at 10:00 a.m., and the Planning Commission gathers on Thursday, August 20, at 5:30 p.m. On the entertainment front, Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, and Grupo Yndio will perform at the Fox Theater on August 22, followed by Rodney Carrington on August 27, CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on August 28, Willie Barcena on August 29, and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix also on August 29. Finally, the MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA comes to the Fox Theater on September 4.
